newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: OPTIONS -- Philips calls in demand on EOE.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -- Philips calls in demand on EOE.

text.p: Philips options took centre stage on the EOE on Wednesday as investors digested news from U.S. semi-conductor maker Intel on Tuesday, interpreting it as bullish for the whole industry.
Dealers said both private and public investors were in the options market looking to buy Philips calls with strikes at 60 guilders and above and expiries from nearby October to January.
"Interest has picked up in Philips today, people have been reading about semi-conductors in the newspapers and have jumped on the bandwagon," one dealer said.
By mid-afternoon over 8,000 Philips calls had changed hands.
Philips accounted for around 17 percent of total business, the lion's share as usual going to trading on the AEX itself.
The index took nearly 30 percent of total volume with roughly 8,000 calls and 8,000 puts traded by mid-afternoon.
Other contracts attracted only light interest.
Dealers said option market makers were continuing to try and keep the underlying AEX index below 565 points and stop a large volume of contracts being exercised at the expiry on Friday.
Selling pressure could increase pressure on the index, sending it back down to 560 by the end of the week, they added.
